name: Fred Turner
profile: British-born biotech entrepreneur (from Brighouse) who dropped out of Oxford biochemistry, moved to San Francisco and founded Thiel-backed TL BioLabs (cattle genetic tests), later Shield Bio (sepsis/gonorrhea diagnostics, a16z/YC). He co-founded Curative in 2020; it became a leading COVID-19 tester, then pivoted to a $0-copay, $0-deductible employer health plan.
interesting_fact: Curative's health plan has no copays or deductibles; the company says its model achieves a 98% member engagement rate and it now uses AI agents to negotiate 2,000+ provider contracts a week.
deep_cut_fact: As a 17-year-old he built a home DNA lab/PCR device in his bedroom, winning the UK's Young Engineer of the Year and ranking #1 at the 2013 EU Contest for Young Scientists; he was named one of the UK's 100 leading practising scientists.
notes: Lane's industry tag 'FinTech' is a Hurun label; Curative is a health insurer. Co-founded with Isaac Turner (CTO, lane 084). Turner writes op-eds on price transparency - healthcare-cost angle likely appealing. No published press email found.

name: Ahmet Bahadir Ozdemir
profile: Turkish serial entrepreneur who co-founded Airalo, the world's first eSIM store, in 2019 with Canadian Abraham Burak. Airalo sells travel eSIMs for 200+ destinations, passed 20 million users in 2025 and became a unicorn after a $220M CVC-led Series C in July 2025. HQ in Delaware, operational base in Singapore.
interesting_fact: His stated vision: 'make Airalo the biggest telecom company without any spectrum or towers.'
deep_cut_fact: Airalo grew out of a decade working with sailors: he founded Sim4crew, a global SIM card for seafarers (plus ship-tracking tool Vestra and 'lowest-data messenger' Bibi), and saw eSIMs as a chance to disrupt his own physical SIM business.
notes: Goes by 'Bahadir Ozdemir' in press. Sources differ on education (METU business graduate per Diken vs 'college dropout' per Silicon Canals) - avoid. No press email found.
